speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you're an 8-year-old having trouble sleeping and waking up frightened; can you tell me exactly what you see or feel during these episodes? Have you noticed any rapid eye movements or strange vocalizations while you were sleeping?

REQUEST TEST: Sleep_Study

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old female. The patient has been experiencing difficulty sleeping for the past 2 months, with episodes of waking up frightened occurring one to two times per week. During these episodes, she yells and cries but does not seem confused after waking and can be consoled by her parents. The following day, she appears more tired than usual.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Difficulty sleeping with episodes of waking up frightened. I also have Yelling and crying during sleep episodes, Temporary post-episode tiredness, Recollection of bad dreams, Bedtime procrastination. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Pyelonephritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That previous diagnosis of Pyelonephritis seems unusual given your symptoms of frightening awakenings and crying; could you describe the specific content of those bad dreams or if you ever scream without remembering why?

REQUEST TEST: Urinalysis to rule out kidney infection; REQUEST IMAGES: Sleep_study_video_clip.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Night Terror Disorder. Although you mentioned bad dreams, the combination of sudden terrified awakenings, crying, screaming, and feeling tired afterward without recalling the dream is characteristic of night terrors rather than typical nightmares or a kidney infection.
